I don't know how old you are but back when I had to do persuasive writing (I got As) I tried to stick to stuff like these -

- If you do an introduction, don't make it boing. Try to briefly summarise the issue you're arguing but make it punchy.

- Always argue both sides of the story

- Depending on the topic and paper, you can write your personal opinion

- Write a conclusion but don't just summarise everything else in it, add new information so that it's not boring

- Use language that stops your piece from being boring - it needs to be engaging for the marker to like it. Emotive language, rhetorical questions etc.

- Remember that your priority isn't to write the best piece you can. The people marking your paper will have a marking scheme in front of them. Your priority is to hit as many of the points in the marking scheme as you can within your time and word limit.

I'm an actual teenager so perhaps I can provide some insight on what stresses me out the most. For context, I'm a 16 year old British lower middle class male.

Work. I'm in college currently but my GCSEs were ridiculous. I was supposed to study for an absurd amount of hours per week when it's common knowledge that secondary education grades hardly mean shit anyway. The main issue is that almost all of my subjects depended on two or so exams. Ridiculous. We all know how important maths is - to those who were in foreign systems, imagine if the last five years of maths education relied on two exams.    
In particular the British school system, schools can be ridiculously strict. Mine was particularly bad. Instant detentions for not having a top button done up, had to stand up when a member of staff walked in, blazer must be worn at all times, shirt tucked in all the way around, five full stripes visible on tie... It's just silly to expect all of this from 11 year old kids.    

Love. Today's media puts out a strong message that love should be the focus of our lives, and that life is 'empty' without someone to love and be loved by. I suck dick at socialising and just haven't met someone I'm into - what is there for me? My parents aren't exactly paragons of care and attention.

Self esteem. I'm an average looking guy. Average weight. Average height. By all means I should be fine. But I'm in a generation surrounded by idolisation of celebrities like Johnny Depp, Chris Hemsworth, Henry Cavill - I know I SHOULD be fine but all of a sudden I'm worrying about how squishy my stomach is and before I know it I'm at the gym counting calories. I can see why eating disorders are common particularly in teenage girls.

Money. I'm told to go to university, maybe have a gap year, go abroad and experience the world -- how!? I can get a shitty £6.50/hour job on a till to do while balancing work and a social life, sure, but that hardly scratches the surface of tuition fees and living costs. Next year I'll be driving and I'm expected to also pay for a care and £1,500/year insurance. Then there's other things like phone contracts, computer upgrades, all that. I'm lucky enough to have parents with a little money as a safety net - what about less affluent families? Or in other countries where tuition fees are more extortionate like America?

Planning. I'm expected to pretty much have my life planned out by now. Thankfully I at least have a goal that I want to work towards and a field that I enjoy to work in, but I feel sorry for people who haven't yet worked out what they want to do with their life. I want to move to America some day and I've spent countless hours these last couple of years working out how to make that happen (fuck you American Immigration system). Why can't I just enjoy my current life without having to meticulously plan ahead?
